text:
elaine: Quick flag 3: observed weird SSE reorder when client reconnects through the proxy. Node client sees later deltas before earlier ones.
mira: can you paste a tiny repro?
elaine: steps: start a long streaming completion (>1500 tokens), kill the client (SIGINT), reconnect immediately. Node emits seq 8 then 6.
sam: which Node parser are we using now?
elaine: `eventsource-parser@1.3.2` in the SDK. Python's iterator client doesn't show the issue.
kyle: any runtime/proxy evidence?
elaine: yes, raw tcp from runtime shows monotonic seq: 6,7,8. Proxy logs show it delivered 8 then 6. Example: 
```
[runtime] 2026-03-18T15:10:00Z id=xyz chunk seq=6
[runtime] 2026-03-18T15:10:01Z id=xyz chunk seq=7
[proxy] 2026-03-18T15:10:02Z id=xyz deliver seq=8
[proxy] 2026-03-18T15:10:02Z id=xyz deliver seq=6
```
elaine: dumping TCP traces indicates the proxy reattached buffered bytes from a previous backend connection after opening a new one.
mira: any auth flow in the middle? we had a token TTL rollback in staging recently.
elaine: Good catch 3: the AuthRelay middleware does a background refresh and opens a new backend connection while draining the old one. That handoff appears to allow both connections' buffers to be merged into the client socket stream.
sam: so root cause is proxy handoff + parser behavior. If the proxy interleaves bytes, naive SSE parsers can emit events out of order based on chunk arrival.
kyle: immediate mitigations: 1) proxy should never merge inflight backend buffers for one client stream; ensure handoff waits for drain or uses an explicit resume token. 2) client SDKs should avoid parallel reconnects for the same stream id.
elaine: agreed. Proposed quick fixes:
- Proxy: add `X-Chunk-Seq` per chunk and `X-Resume-Token` on stream start so clients can detect/ask to resume after a given seq.
- Node SDK: debounce reconnect attempts (200-300ms) and switch to a strict event-boundary parser that only emits on full event (\u2014\u2014 two newlines).
- Python SDK: add `allow_resume=True` and `resume_after` param to `stream()` so caller can opt into resume semantics.
sam: I'd like the Node SDK patch to also include a small verifier that checks in-payload `seq` field and discards out-of-order emits (while logging) to avoid app-level surprises.
mira: can we also add an integration test in devex/samples that simulates a forced token refresh/reconnect and asserts monotonic seq consumption?
kyle: yes, add test under `devex/samples/streaming-handshake` that toggles auth TTL.
elaine: question about UX: should reconnect mid-stream be considered an error by default? If we fail fast apps get a deterministic retry surface. If we resume, apps get resilience but must handle duplicate partials.
sam: default to one resume attempt then fail with a clear code `stream_resume_failed`. Provide `fail_fast=True` opt-in for deterministic apps.
elaine: I'll draft a PR for Node: replace parser + add reconnect debounce + opt-in seq-guard.
elaine: PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/490 (WIP)
mira: infra: can you schedule a quick proxy handoff audit? we need to ensure handoff drains before merge or uses resume token flow.
infra-bot: Audit created INFRA-732: proxy stream handoff review. ETA 2026-03-19 14:00 UTC.
elaine: filed bug ENG-STREAM-1133 with tcp dump and repro script. cc @kyle @sam.
sam: docs note: recommend streaming token TTL > expected duration and show pattern for proactive refresh vs fail-fast.
kyle: also add server-side invariant: chunk seq must be strictly increasing for a given stream id; runtime should drop/sequence-check on replay.
mira: small parser nit: ensure we never split inside `data:` lines. If proxy can split, client parsers must buffer incomplete lines until a full \"\n\n\" event terminator is seen.
elaine: Node patch will implement a tiny stateful parser that keeps partial lines. That should fix emission order even if proxy occasionally splits at an arbitrary byte.
sam: follow-ups: ENG-STREAM-1133 (bug), INFRA-732 (audit), sdk-node PR 490, sdk-python resume PR.
elaine: thanks all. I'll push the Node WIP and add the sample harness.
elaine: :thumbsup:
sam: closing out 3: if infra confirms proxy merges are the cause we'll prefer a proxy fix; otherwise ship SDK mitigations first.
